in_hebrew.name: יואקימה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם יואקימה מורכב מהשורשים העבריים 'יוא' ו'קימה', שפירושם 'האלוהים יקים או יעמיד'. השם קשור קשר הדוק לנבואה המקראית ולמילוי רצון אלוהים. הוא משמש לעתים קרובות בהקשר של התחייה או ההעמדה של אלוהים, ומשקף אמונה בריבונותו ובפעולתו בחיי המאמינים.

in_greek.name: Ιωακείμα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιωακείμα προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές ρίζες 'Ιω' και 'ακείμα', που σημαίνουν 'Θεός αναστήσει ή στηρίξει'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη και την πρώιμη Εκκλησία, το όνομα συνδέθηκε με την προφητεία και την εκπλήρωση του θελήματος του Θεού. Αντικατοπτρίζει την πίστη στην κυριαρχία και την παρέμβαση του Θεού στη ζωή των πιστών.

in_latin.name: Joakima
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Joakima ex radicibus Latinis 'Deus' et 'eximius' vel 'constituet' derivatur, quae significant 'Deus eximius vel constituet'. In Ecclesia primitiva et traditione Christiana, nomen Joakima ad prophetiam et effectum voluntatis divinae referebatur. Significat fidem in dominio et actione Dei in vita fidelium.

in_english.name: Joakima
in_english.long_meaning: The name Joakima originates from Hebrew roots 'Yoa' and 'qumah', meaning 'God will raise or establish'. It is connected to biblical prophecy and the fulfillment of God's will. Historically, the name has been used in Christian tradition to signify faith in God's sovereignty and action in the lives of believers. It reflects spiritual themes of resurrection, divine support, and providence.

data.cultural_impact: The name Joakima is rich in cultural history, particularly in Eastern Orthodox Christianity. Saint Joakima of Tyre is one of the most revered saints in this tradition. She was a Palestinian-Syrian Christian princess who was forced into a tower near the seacoast as a child in order to conceal her from Roman persecution. Throughout her years of isolation, she dedicated her time in prayer and fasting. Eventually, her tower was discovered, and she was accused of being a witch. She was sent to Rome for trial, where she was subjected to various forms of torture. Despite her suffering, she remained steadfast in her faith. Her miracles through these trials became the basis of her sainthood, and she is now venerated as the patron saint of midwives.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Joakima is deeply spiritual in meaning, conveying the sense of God's presence and healing power. It serves as a reminder that even in times of isolation or suffering, one can turn to God for strength and solace. The name also reflects the Biblical themes of faithfulness, endurance, and the importance of maintaining one's spiritual connection with God, no matter the circumstances.
